text:
RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 3

The woman who got the job is, like you, a woman. An all-female panel choosing a female candidate over another female candidate tells you nothing about sex bias against you — there's no differential treatment by sex to point at. Raising it would likely read as grievance-driven and damage your standing in a field where reputations travel.

The real anomaly is substantive: you hold a master's and a licence; she holds a bachelor's. That suggests the panel weighted consultation and stakeholder skills heavily — plausibly because the role is politically exposed, or because an internal/known candidate was favoured.

Chase the written feedback: polite follow-up to HR, cite your request date, ask specifically which criteria you scored lower on.
